title: Approval Processes & Advanced Approvals
source: ../Salesforce CPQ & Revenue cloud/Salesforce CPQ  & Revenue Cloud Roadmap/developer CPQ & Revenue Cloud Roadmap/07-Approvals-and-Advanced-Approvals.md

toc.text: Hands-on walkthrough: route discount approvals by threshold

html:
Quotes carry money, and money must be governed. Approval Processes & Advanced Approvals give CPQ admins the controls that decide who has to bless what before a quote can go to the customer. In the CPQ & Revenue Cloud Academy model this shows up on the Quote.Approval_Status__c field, in the Approval_Log__c audit trail, and in the ApprovalRoutingService Apex service. It is a compact but exam-critical domain: Approvals = 4% of the Certified CPQ Specialist blueprint, and approval design is a top implementation-readiness question in the Revenue Cloud Consultant exam.

This guide covers approval rules, approval matrices, approval chains, sequential vs parallel routing, and the advanced options — delegation, escalation, self-approval, and auto-approval — then walks through routing discount approvals by threshold on the academy data model.

Learning objectives

  • Explain why quote approval exists as a control point and how it gates the rest of quote-to-cash.
  • Distinguish approval rules, approval conditions, and approval matrices.
  • Build approval matrices that map quote attributes to the correct approver.
  • Configure approval chains and control when a child line inherits the parent's approval state.
  • Compare sequential vs parallel (advanced) approval and know when each fits.
  • Use approval routing fields such as Approval_Status__c and the Approval_Log__c audit object.
  • Set up escalation, delegation, reminders, and auto-approval options.
  • Carry a quote's approval into contracts, orders, and billing so no unapproved deal leaks downstream.

Why approvals gate the pipeline

A rep who can set any discount at any time is a liability. Approvals exist to enforce commercial policy: "discounts above 15% need the regional VP," "special pricing on the enterprise tier needs the finance director." The approval layer turns those policies into an enforced workflow instead of an email thread.

Approvals also create a clean state machine on the quote. A quote typically moves through draft → submitted → in approval → approved → rejected. Only an approved quote can generate a contract or an order; a rejected quote sends the rep back to fix pricing or terms. That state machine is exactly what downstream automation reads:

Quote.Approval_Status__cMeaningDownstream effect
DraftBeing built, not yet submittedNothing downstream is allowed
SubmittedSent into routingApproval process owns it
ApprovedEvery required approver said yesContract/Order generation allowed
RejectedAt least one approver said noQuote returns to rep; no downstream allowed

Approval rules and conditions

The simplest form of approval is a rule: when a condition is true, route the quote to a specific approver or approval group. Rules are evaluated when the quote is submitted, and all matching rules contribute to the routing. A rule has fields for the condition (record type, territory, product family, field value) and the action (assign to a user, role, or queue).

A classic rule set for discount governance looks like this:

When this is trueRoute to
Discount_Percent__c <= 10 and opportunity under $50kAuto-approve
Discount_Percent__c > 10 and <= 20Sales Manager
Discount_Percent__c > 20Regional VP
Any quote flagged Is_Strategic__c = trueVP Sales + Finance

Conditions are free-form and can reference the quote, the account, the opportunity, and per-line aggregates. The moment you need a matrix — different approvals for different combinations of account segment and discount band — you graduate from rules to an approval matrix.

Approval matrices

An approval matrix is the high-water mark of rule-based approvals: rows and columns define intersections, and the cell tells you the approver or approval chain for that intersection. Matrices are ideal for discount governance because deals are usually shaped by two or three dimensions rather than a single field.

Discount ≤ 10%10% < Discount ≤ 20%Discount > 20%
Enterprise / StrategicAuto-approveVP SalesVP Sales + CFO
Mid-MarketAuto-approveSales ManagerRegional VP
SMBAuto-approveSales ManagerSales Manager + Finance

CPQ implements matrices on records whose rows and columns carry the threshold values; the engine finds the cell for the quote's attributes and resolves the approver. Because the thresholds live in data, not in code, you can tune governance without a deployment — which is why the academy model keeps a Discount_Schedule__c-style data object and a separate Approval_Log__c audit trail.

Approval chains and parents

An approval chain is an ordered list of approvers: approver 1 acts first, and only when they approve does the next approver see the quote. Chains model escalating authority — team lead, then manager, then VP — and are the natural way to express "the bigger the number, the more signatures."

When a quote has bundle lines, the parent/child relationship matters. A parent line's approval state applies to the whole bundle: approving the parent implies the children are handled, and routing typically acts on the parent so the approver does not approve the same bundle line by line. On the academy data model the line attributes Is_Bundle_Parent__c and Bundle_Option__c identify which lines are bundle structure versus real sellable lines, so your approval logic can act on parents only.

apex
// ApprovalRoutingService: resolve approver for a quote by discount band
public class ApprovalRoutingService {
    public static String resolveApprover(Quote quote, Decimal discount) {
        if (discount <= 10) {
            return 'Auto-Approved';                    // rule 1: no human approver
        } else if (discount <= 20) {
            return 'Sales Manager';
        } else if (quote.Is_Strategic) {
            return 'VP Sales + CFO';                   // matrix cell (strategic, high)
        }
        return 'Regional VP';
    }
}

Sequential vs advanced (parallel) approval

Standard approval routes one approver at a time. Advanced approvals fan out so several approvers can act at once. Sequencing matters because it models the dependencies in your governance, not just who signs:

  • Sequential — approver B does not see the quote until approver A approves. Use when approval is a hierarchy or when a later approver's input depends on an earlier decision.
  • Parallel — A and B receive the quote simultaneously; the quote needs both (or either). Use when signatures are independent — sales and legal can review at the same time and cut your approval lead time in half.
ConcernSequentialParallel
Typical useEscalating discount tiersSales ops + Legal review
Wall-clock timeLongestShorter
Decision dependencyStrongWeak
Aborts first rejectionYesEach branch independently

Advanced approval options also include escalation (if no action in N days, route to the next level), reminders, delegation, self-approval (if the approver is also the submitter), and auto-approval for surrogates — when an approver is out of office, a delegate can act with a recorded rationale.

The audit trail: Approval_Log__c

Approval is only trustworthy if it is auditable. Every decision in the academy model lands on Approval_Log__c, which stores the quote, the approval type, the approver, the decision, the discount in play, comments, and the decision date. This object answers the questions auditors and Revenue Cloud consultants actually care about:

  • Was the discount above the finance threshold approved, and by whom?
  • How long did approval take?
  • At what approval stage was the deal rejected, and with what comments?
soql
SELECT Quote__c, Approval_Type__c, Approver__c, Decision__c,
       Discount_Percent__c, Comments__c, Decision_Date__c
FROM Approval_Log__c
WHERE Quote__c = '00Q6g000000XyAb'
ORDER BY Decision_Date__c DESC
💡
Tip: Never delete approval logs. They are your defense when a deal gets audited or when a signed discount is later disputed at the invoice stage.

Approvals in Revenue Cloud / RLM

Revenue Cloud re-grounds the same concepts on core platform building blocks: approval steps and approval processes built on the Lightning platform, with CPQ attributes (discount, total, margin) feeding the entry criteria. The administrative surface differs from the legacy SBQQ__ model, but the exam facts and the governance intent are identical.

Whatever the flavor, keep three rules in mind: approvals gate quote-to-cash progression, chains express escalation, and the log is the source of truth.

text
Draft -> Submitted -> (matrix resolves approver) -> Approved / Rejected
    ^                                            |
    +---------------- fix pricing <--------------+

Hands-on walkthrough: route discount approvals by threshold

This walkthrough uses the academy Quote, QuoteLineItem, Approval_Log__c records and the ApprovalRoutingService Apex service.

  1. Pick a quote (or create one) with Approval_Status__c = 'Draft' and note its Discount_Percent__c.
  2. Map the policy in your head: ≤ 10 auto-approve; ≤ 20 Sales Manager; > 20 Regional VP unless Is_Strategic__c, then VP Sales + CFO.
  3. Submit the quote and confirm the service evaluated the threshold:
apex
Quote q = [SELECT Id, Discount_Percent__c, Is_Strategic__c
           FROM Quote WHERE Id = :theQuoteId];
String approver = ApprovalRoutingService.resolveApprover(q, q.Discount_Percent__c);
System.debug('Routing to: ' + approver);
  1. Insert the approver decision into Approval_Log__c for the walkthrough — in production the approval process does this:
apex
insert new Approval_Log__c(
    Quote__c            = q.Id,
    Approval_Type__c    = 'Discount',
    Approver__c         = approver,
    Decision__c         = 'Approved',
    Discount_Percent__c = q.Discount_Percent__c,
    Comments__c         = 'Within threshold, approved.',
    Decision_Date__c    = System.today()
);
  1. Update the quote to Approval_Status__c = 'Approved' and record CPQ_Quote_Status__c on the Opportunity.
  2. Repeat with a quote at 25% discount on a strategic opportunity and confirm the chain selects VP Sales + CFO (a two-step sequential chain). Act as approver 1, then approver 2, and confirm the quote only becomes Approved after both log decisions.
  3. Simulate a rejection (set Decision__c = 'Rejected', Comments__c the reason), move the quote back to Draft, and verify the rejection appears first in the Approval_Log__c query above.
  4. Verify no contract or order generation service will run on a quote that is not Approved — the gate is real, and the walkthrough should confirm the guard clause.

Common pitfalls

  • Approving non-parent lines — routing child bundle lines individually bloats the queue; act on parents (Is_Bundle_Parent__c) and let the bundle inherit.
  • Bypassing the auto-approve band — every deal under the threshold still needs a decision; without an explicit "auto-approve" rule the quote hangs in limbo.
  • No rejection reason — a rejected quote with no Comments__c forces the rep to guess; make comments mandatory on rejection.
  • One matrix to rule them all — a single global matrix can't model regional or product-line policy; use several matrices scoped by record type or territory.
  • Making everything parallel — parallel routing is great for independent sign-offs but wrong for escalating discount chains; mix sequential and parallel deliberately.
  • Deleting the log — you lose the audit trail and any chance of defending the price on the invoice.

Key takeaways

  • Approval is the enforcement layer for commercial policy and the gate that keeps unapproved deals out of contracts, orders, and billing.
  • Rules handle simple "if this, route to that"; matrices handle the multidimensional discount-approval reality.
  • Chains express escalation and parent/child inheritance keeps bundle approvals clean.
  • Sequential vs parallel is a dependency decision, not a style preference.
  • Approval_Log__c is the audit trail that makes approvals defensible; treat it as immutable.
  • The same governance intent — approve by threshold, escalate by amount, log every decision — carries over to Revenue Cloud / RLM.
